disagreements.theirs: a source that earns its bar earns a place; two records is a mashup, which is a form

disagreements.about: whether the bass line is a part or the song's floor
disagreements.position: the bass is the floor everything else is judged against, and one line is enough
disagreements.settledBy: churn: past four versions of the line the Producer calls it
disagreements.theirs: the line is written to the kick and the key and is its own part with its own versions

disagreements.about: whether loudness is a decision or a delivery spec
disagreements.position: the level is a delivery spec and the last thing decided
disagreements.settledBy: the Engineer reads every bounce; the Producer decides at the last one
disagreements.theirs: the level is heard from the first bounce and shapes every choice after it

disagreements.about: whether the outside ear outranks the brief
disagreements.position: the brief is the song's; the Peer's ear is a reading, not a ruling
disagreements.settledBy: the Peer's readings are heard; the Producer says which change the brief
disagreements.theirs: the listener never reads the brief and only hears the song

disagreements.about: whether the words serve the brief or the brief serves the words
disagreements.position: the brief is one sentence and the words are measured against it
disagreements.settledBy: the title: if the Lyricist's hook line and the brief disagree, the brief is rewritten, once
disagreements.theirs: the song is about what the words say it is about, once they are sung

lineages.name: Rick Rubin
lineages.why: The method is stated as method: reduce until the song breaks and then put one thing back; ask what the song is about before what it needs; hold the artist's attention on the thing that matters. The Creative Act is a whole book of it, the American Recordings are the demonstration — one voice and one guitar — and the interviews repeat the same three moves.

lineages.name: Brian Eno
lineages.why: Process over taste, written down twice. The Oblique Strategies are a procedure for getting unstuck without first deciding what good is; the 1995 diary records the procedure in use on real records, with the sessions dated. A lineage whose method is a deck of cards can be checked card by card.

lineages.instrument: the tape machine, and a written contract
lineages.name: Steve Albini
lineages.why: The refusals are published and specific: the recording is a document of the band, the engineer takes no points and makes no artistic decisions, the budget is one sentence. The Nirvana letter is the whole position in four pages, and In Utero is the record it produced.

name: Producer

openQuestions.alternative: A ceiling per idiom — a lo-fi beat at four, a produced pop record at twelve — with the brief naming the idiom and the ceiling following it.
openQuestions.encoded: Eight, from the sparse end of the lineages: Cash at two, Bowie's Low at five to eight, In Utero at four to six.

evidence.inferred: three lineages' records counted by ear

openQuestions.question: Is eight the right ceiling on parts, or is it idiom-dependent?

openQuestions.alternative: Churn is not a count but a shape — versions that move less each time — and the rule should read the size of the change, not the number of them.
openQuestions.encoded: Four: Eno's diary rarely records more than three passes at a thing before the question changes.
openQuestions.question: Is four versions churn, or is it work?

openQuestions.alternative: In a sample idiom the parts are inside the chop, and reduction applies to slices and layers rather than to parts — the Sampler's density is the Producer's count.
openQuestions.encoded: Yes: a chop, a groove and a bass line is three parts, and a fourth is the question.
openQuestions.question: Does Rubin's reduction apply to sample-based music, where the parts are already few?

openQuestions.alternative: Every no is a decision, and the honest position is that the Producer is the only persona allowed one — which is why it must write the brief down first.
openQuestions.encoded: The Producer holds the brief and says no; the artist decides. The call is a reading of the brief, not a preference.
openQuestions.question: If the engineer makes no artistic decisions, is the Producer's call an artistic decision?
